testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which item is not acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: For vehicle inspection, you must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares. You also need a properly charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When checking brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster after setting wheel chocks and releasing the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to make sure it does not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing the brake pedal activates an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours will usually:

options.text: Take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Take about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can usually stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far back to follow other vehicles.

questions.question: If you are not sure if the road is becoming icy, you can:

options.text: Open your window and feel the front of the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the front of the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icy but are not sure, open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they:
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and loads shift easily. Be careful when turning and taking curves.

questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: If equipped, the trailer brake hand valve can stop the vehicle from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, exiting your vehicle incorrectly will result in:

options.text: An extra point against your final score.
Automatic failure of the entire test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the entire test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: When should you test parking brakes?

options.text: Only after you have driven some distance.

questions.explanation: Always check your parking brakes before you drive. This is part of your pre-trip inspection. If the parking brakes do not hold your vehicle in place, the vehicle needs to be repaired before you drive.

questions.question: How long do you have to tell your employer about a traffic conviction?
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days if you are convicted of any traffic violation. You must also inform your motor vehicle agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. Parking tickets do not need to be reported.

questions.question: During inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, check your brake drums during your walk-around inspection. It is unsafe to drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: Which of these is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air becomes old and needs replacing.
Because compressed air contains water that can damage the brakes.
To remove bad air from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that can damage the brakes.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. These can build up and damage the brakes. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should you activate four-way flashers?

options.text: Only if a train is approaching.

questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers while approaching and crossing railroad tracks. Turn them off after your entire vehicle has crossed the tracks.

questions.question: Which surface gives the least traction?
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: Why is it most important to inspect your vehicle before driving?

options.text: To keep yourself and others safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep yourself and others safe.
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle before driving is safety. Pre-trip safety inspections are required by state and federal laws to protect you and other drivers.

questions.question: Which of these could prevent you from getting a hazmat endorsement?

options.text: Not being a lawful permanent U.S. resident.
Having a speeding ticket in the last three years.
Missing one question on the hazmat test.
Not passing the hazmat test on your first try.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not being a lawful permanent U.S. resident.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazmat endorsement if you are not a lawful permanent U.S. resident, give up U.S. citizenship, have certain felony convictions, are judged mentally defective, or are considered a security threat by the TSA.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how much does brake lag add to stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The brakes will not work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.explanation: When the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, jackknifing risk goes down. The driver can still steer the vehicle. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle plus its load
The total weight of the tractor only
The total weight of a loaded trailer
The weight of a tractor and trailer without the load

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle plus its load
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle and everything it is carrying.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should inspect it:

options.text: Only at the start of the trip
Only after driving a long distance

questions.explanation: Check your cargo and tie-downs before you start driving. After you begin, check them within the first 50 miles, then every three hours or 150 miles. Also check them after every break.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes
Should turn off within a few seconds
Should stay on until you turn them off

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and ABS should turn off right away.

questions.question: The two things that tell you when to upshift are:

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure

questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual for the right rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work with each gear and watch the speedometer to shift up when needed.

questions.question: Fuel records for IFTA quarterly tax returns must be kept for:
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles used in interstate commerce must be registered under the International Registration Plan (IRP) and International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA). These programs collect registration fees and fuel taxes. You must keep fuel and mileage records for four years.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes
The temperature of the air in the brake system
The pressure of air from the compressor
How many times the brakes have been used

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all air brake systems have this gauge.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a type of tie-down equipment?
questions.explanation: Proper tie-downs are needed to secure cargo on flatbed trailers. Examples include ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: Look ahead ____ of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot and react to hazards before you reach them. Look for vehicles entering the highway or changing into your lane.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge is too high, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check for problems

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check for problems
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the safe level, stop driving as soon as you can and find the problem. High coolant temperature can cause engine failure and possibly a fire.

questions.question: How can you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake. Use the parking brake if needed to prevent rolling backward.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black from dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet but is actually icy.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you need to identify all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for tightness, cracks, or fraying. If any of these are not belt-driven, tell the examiner and check that they work properly, are mounted securely, and are not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
The driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. Examples include those with ice on windshields, those with large items blocking windows, and those driving rental trucks unfamiliar with limited rear visibility.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. The valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you spend too much time looking at a single mirror?

options.text: Looking at mirrors can make you drowsy.
It can cause you to drive a long distance without looking at the road.
The mirror may not show the road accurately.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause you to drive a long distance without looking at the road.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors often but quickly. Staring at one mirror for too long means you're not watching the road ahead for a long distance.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: For transit buses, school buses, or placarded vehicles at railroad crossings: Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing.

questions.question: How often should you stop for a break while driving to avoid getting tired?
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, stop for a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: On a leaf spring, the leaves:
questions.explanation: Check leaf springs for broken or missing leaves. This is dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must not be driven.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is involved in a crash ahead, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely past the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely past the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash with an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation (not a parking ticket), you must:

options.text: Put a sign on your vehicle about the conviction.
Lose your CDL for six months.

questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, check the hoses for:

options.text: If they are connected to the battery.
If they have the right amount of slack.

questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: To do a standard parallel park, you should:

options.text: Back past the space, then pull forward into it.
Drive past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your right. Then back into it slowly, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be fully within the space.

questions.question: A 40-foot load must be secured by at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: Why are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly

questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, you should NOT:

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle is on fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and report the fire and your location.

questions.question: What is an encroachment during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake.
The vehicle touching a boundary line.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:

options.text: Loose and easy to slide off.

questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. Each belt should have the right amount of tightness for your vehicle.
